issues.description: Imports.Directs still dereferences i.publicEnd inside closure when receiver was nil
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go, Directs() guards the slice with a nil check but the inner closure still references `i.publicEnd` and `i.weakEnd`. With a nil `*imports`, the slice is empty so the closure won't be invoked, but the closure captures `i` and any future caller that iterates a non-empty slice with i==nil would panic. Consider asserting the invariant or capturing locals.

issues.description: DescriptorProto on nil receiver inconsistent with IsDescriptorProto semantics
issues.detail: imports.DescriptorProto() returns nil when i==nil, but File.IsDescriptorProto() returns false for nil File. A nil File whose session/imports tree is partially populated could still call IsDescriptorProto via InternedPath which itself isn't nil-guarded. The nil-guard pattern is inconsistent across the file — some accessors guard, others (InternedPath, InternedPackage, Path, Package) don't, which the test doesn't cover since it only tests *ir.File zero (which is a nil pointer, not a zero struct).

issues.description: Zero-test reflection skips methods returning functions and may give false confidence
issues.detail: In zero_test.go testZeroAny, when a return value's Kind is reflect.Func the loop `continue`s, skipping the zero check entirely. This means iter.Seq returns (e.g. AllMembers) are not verified to be safe-to-iterate; the test would pass even if calling the returned iterator panicked. Consider invoking the iterator with a no-op yield to actually exercise it.

issues.description: Reflection test only covers exported methods with no arguments, missing many accessors
issues.detail: The filter `NumIn() != 1` skips every method that takes parameters (e.g. ImportFor(that *File)). The PR description claims comprehensive zero coverage, but methods like File.ImportFor are not validated against nil receivers. Either document this limitation or add explicit cases for parameterized accessors.

issues.description: Repeated nil-guard boilerplate could be extracted
issues.detail: ir_file.go now has ~10 nearly identical `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field } return seq.NewFixedSlice(x, ...)` blocks. A small helper like `safeSlice(f, func(f *File) []T)` would reduce duplication and make future fields harder to forget. Not blocking, but the pattern is now load-bearing and worth consolidating.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex sentinel of -1 is a behavior change worth noting in CHANGELOG
issues.detail: Element.ValueNodeIndex() previously would panic or return whatever the search produced; now it silently returns -1 for the zero element. Callers that previously assumed a non-negative result (e.g. used it directly as a slice index) will now index with -1 and panic at the caller. The docstring is updated but downstream callers should be audited.

review.summary: The PR adds defensive nil/zero guards to many IR accessors and a reflection-based test that exercises zero values. The approach is sound and the test is a nice forcing function, but the reflection test has gaps — it skips methods returning functions (so iter.Seq results aren't actually iterated) and skips all parameterized accessors, which limits the safety guarantee it advertises. The nil-guard pattern is also applied inconsistently across ir_file.go (some accessors like InternedPath/Package/Path are not guarded) and the repetition of the boilerplate suggests extracting a helper. No P0 blockers; recommend tightening the test and auditing remaining unguarded accessors before merge.
